speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To narrow this down, can you tell me how many days ago your symptoms started and if anyone around you is currently sick?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola infantum (Exanthema subitum). The onset of a high fever followed by a pruritic rash after several days, alongside viral prodrome symptoms like rhinorrhea and headache, is classic for this condition, which is typically caused by HHV-6.
